«مقتا» is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent, i.e. "the hatred of their disputing is grievous". Here is the wording of al-Samīn: "«كبر مقتا» may be meant as wonder and deeming-great, and it may be meant as censure like «بئس»; that is because a verb of the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the middle radical may be formed from what permits wonder, and it takes the course of «نعم» and «بئس» in all rulings, and its agent has six aspects" until he says: "The second, that it refers to their disputing understood from «يجادلون» as above" until he says: "The fifth, that the agent is a pronoun referring to what comes after, which is the tamyīz, as in 'what an excellent man Zayd' and 'what a bad boy ʿAmr'; and «عند الله» is an adverbial attached to «كبر»." «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "like that sealing"; «يطبع الله»: an imperfect verb and an agent; «على كل قلب» is attached to «يطبع»; «قلب» is a muḍāf and «متكبر» a muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "upon every heart of a proud person"; and «جبار» is a second adjective.

* Benefits:
1- A valuable discussion:
Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that «من» in «من هو مسرف» was treated according to its form and then according to its meaning. The Arabists found this strange, because it contains vagueness after clarification, and this is unbecoming to the Qur'an's eloquence, since the rhetoricians hold the reverse. The correct view is to make the pronoun in «كبر» refer to the maṣdar of the preceding verb, namely «يجادلون», its implied form being "their disputing is grievous in hatred", and to make «الذين» a mubtadaʾ on the interpretation of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "the disputing of those who dispute about the verses of Allah", the pronoun in «كبر مقتا» referring to the omitted «الجدال»; the clause is a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Similar in omitting the annexed maṣdar and building the speech on it is the saying of the Exalted: «أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله», according to one of its two interpretations, and there are many like it.
2- «كل قلب»:
«كل» is for the generality of misguidance of the heart as a whole, not for the generality of hearts, i.e. misguidance encompassed all parts of the heart, so that no place of guidance remained in it. It is well known that when «كل» enters an indefinite noun absolutely, or a plural definite noun, it is for the generality of individuals, and when it enters a singular definite noun it is for the generality of parts; here the non-genuine annexation (ghayr maḥḍa) was treated as the genuine annexation.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حم): what has been said about it at the beginning of the sūras suffices, and we add here what al-Jawharī said: «آل حم are sūras in the Qur'an; as for the saying of the common people "al-ḥawāmīm", it is not from the speech of the Arabs.» Abū ʿUbayda said: «"al-ḥawāmīm" are sūras in the Qur'an, contrary to the regular pattern.» He said: «It is better to form the plural as "dhawāt ḥā-mīm".» The upshot is that these seven sūras are called al-ḥawāmīm, and called āl ḥā-mīm, and called dhawāt ḥā-mīm. So they have three plurals, contrary to al-Jawharī who denied the first. Al-Kumayt said, praising the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt):
وجدنا لكم في آل حم آية ... تأولها منا تقي ومعرب
(We found for you in āl ḥā-mīm a verse; the God-fearing and the eloquent among us interpreted it.)
It means "dhawāt", that is, in the sūras attributed to this expression. It is known that the word آل, just as it is applied to "family", is also applied in the sense of ذو (possessor of); so it is placed before compound names and the like that cannot be put in the dual or plural, such as تأبط شرا. When they wish to make it dual or plural, and it is a sentence in which that cannot be done, and nothing like it is known in the speech of the Arabs, they add before it the word آل or ذو and say: جاءني آل تأبط شرا or ذو تأبط شرا, meaning the two men or the men so named. From this comes آل حم in the sense of al-ḥawāmīm in al-Kumayt's verse mentioned above.
(التَّوْبِ): in al-Mukhtār: «التوب is the turning back from sin, and its pattern is "qāla"; also توبة.» Al-Akhfash said: «التوب is the plural of توبة, like دوم and دومة.»
(الطَّوْلِ): excess, abundance and wide-ranging bounty. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ:
«الطول with fatḥa is favour (al-mann); from it one says طال يطول (pattern "qāla") when he bestowed a favour on him.» Al-Māwardī said: «The difference between al-mann and al-faḍl is that al-mann is pardon for a sin, while al-tafaḍḍul is beneficence that is not deserved.»

* I'rab:
(حم، تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ): the i'rab of the openings of the sūras has been discussed. The easiest of it is that they are the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is what follows. تنزيل الكتاب is a mubtadaʾ and من الله its khabar, and العزيز العليم are two adjectives. (غافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقابِلِ التَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ الْعِقابِ ذِي الطَّوْلِ): these too are adjectives of the Majestic Name; what has been said about the difference between some adjectives and the described, in respect of definiteness and indefiniteness, will come in the section on benefits. (لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ إِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ): it is possible that this sentence is an adjective, as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, but it is objected that a sentence cannot be an adjective of definite nouns; he may have meant that it is an adjective of شديد العقاب. It is better that it be a resumptive sentence, or an inseparable ḥāl. The i'rab of the word of testimony has been given in detail earlier. إليه is a fronted khabar and المصير a postponed mubtadaʾ. (ما يُجادِلُ فِي آياتِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): ما is negative; يجادل is an imperfect nominative verb; في آيات الله are two [elements] attached to يجادل; إلا is a particle of restriction; الذين is the agent; and the clause كفروا is a ṣila. (فَلا يَغْرُرْكَ تَقَلُّبُهُمْ فِي الْبِلادِ): the فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); لا is prohibitive; يغررك is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; the ك is a direct object; تقلبهم is the agent; and في البلاد are two [elements] attached to تقلبهم. The meaning: if it is established with you that those who dispute about the signs of Allah are disbelievers, then do not be deceived by their going about in the land with profitable trading, for they are seized for their disbelief.
(كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَالْأَحْزابُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): كذبت is a past verb and the ت is for the feminine; قبلهم is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; قوم نوح is the agent; الأحزاب is conjoined to قوم نوح, and they are the people of ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh and others; and من بعدهم are two [elements] attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَهَمَّتْ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ لِيَأْخُذُوهُ): وهمت is conjoined to كذبت; كل أمة is the agent; برسولهم are two [elements] attached to همت; the لام is causal; يأخذوه is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām, the و is the agent and the ه the direct object. The meaning of ليأخذوه is "so that they might be able to inflict [harm] upon him". (وَجادَلُوا بِالْباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الْحَقَّ فَأَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كانَ عِقابِ): «وحاولوا» is conjoined to همت [Translator's note: the source says «وحاولوا», though the verse reads «وجادلوا»; translated as written]; بالباطل are two [elements] attached to an omitted ḥāl; ليدحضوا: the lām is causal, and يدحضوا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām; به are two [elements] attached to يدحضوا; and الحق is the direct object. فأخذتهم is conjoined to جادلوا. فكيف: the فاء is a conjunction; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a fronted khabar of كان; and عقاب is the noun of كان, nominative, its nominative marker being an implied ḍamma on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, following the orthography of the muṣḥaf.
(وَكَذلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ): the كاف may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar — this has been established more than once — and it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and the matter is thus". كلمة ربك is the agent; على الذين كفروا are two [elements] attached to حقت. أنهم أصحاب النار: the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of nominative as a badal of كلمة ربك, or in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, which is the causal lām.

* Benefits:
1- Difference between the described and the adjective:
Among the weighty topics of grammar is the occurrence of an apparent difference between the described and the adjective. Someone might say: how is it permissible to describe a definite noun, namely Allah the Glorified, with غافر الذنب, قابل التوب and شديد العقاب, since these three are derived forms, and the annexation of a derived form does not give it definiteness? Hence the difference referred to arises. Sībawayh answered this with his saying: «Everything whose annexation is not genuine may be made genuine and used to describe definite nouns, except the assimilated adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha).» As for the Kufans, they did not except the assimilated adjective either, saying of the like of حسن الوجه that its annexation can become genuine. On their view all three can be adjectives; on Sībawayh's view, شديد العقاب is parsed as a badal. Here is al-Zamakhsharī's account on this point. He said: «If you ask: how do these adjectives differ in definiteness and indefiniteness, when the described is definite and requires that its like be definite? I say: as for غافر الذنب and قابل التوب, they are definite, because by them He did not mean the occurrence of the two acts, that He forgives sin and accepts repentance now or tomorrow, so that they would be in the sense of separable [from the time], making their annexation non-genuine; rather He meant the permanence and continuity of that. So their ruling is that of إله الخلق and رب العرش. As for شديد العقاب, its case is problematic, because it is in the sense of "severe in his punishment", which cannot be detached from this sense. Al-Zajjāj made it a badal, but its being a badal alone among the adjectives is an evident awkwardness. The right way is to say: since this one indefinite was met among these definites, it signals that all of them are badals, not adjectives. Like this is a poem all of whose feet come on mustafʿilun: it is judged to be of the meter rajaz; but if one foot of it occurs on mutafāʿilun, it is of the kāmil. Someone could also say that they are adjectives, and the alif and lām were dropped from شديد العقاب to balance what precedes and follows it in wording; they have altered much of their speech from its rules for the sake of balance... Moreover al-Khalīl said, on their saying ما يحسن بالرجل مثلك أن يفعل ذلك and ما يحسن بالرجل خير منك أن يفعل كذا, that it is with the intention of alif and lām, just as الجماء الغفير is with the intention of dropping the alif and lām; and what made this easy is that confusion is not feared and the described is not unknown. It may also be said that He deliberately made it indefinite and vague to indicate extreme severity, and that nothing is more calamitous or bitter than it, to increase the warning. And it may be said that this subtlety is what calls for choosing badal over adjective if you take the route of badals.»
2- The subtlety of the added wāw:
In the added wāw in His saying وقابل التوب there is a weighty subtlety, namely that it conveys the joining of two mercies: forgiveness of sin and acceptance of repentance. It is reported that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb missed a man of great valour from the people of al-Shām, and was told that he had persisted in this drink. ʿUmar said to his scribe: "Write: From ʿUmar to so-and-so. Peace be upon you. I praise Allah, than whom there is no god but He. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. حم" up to His saying «إليه المصير», and he sealed the letter and said to his messenger: "Do not hand it to him until you find him sober." Then he ordered those with him to pray for him to repent. When the letter reached him, he began to read it and say: "Allah has promised me that He will forgive me and has warned me of His punishment", and he kept repeating it until he wept; then he gave it up, and gave it up well, and his repentance was good. When it reached ʿUmar he said: "Do thus, when you see your brother has slipped: set him straight, help him to succeed, and ask Allah to accept his repentance, and do not be helpers of the devils against him." I say:
What ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, did must be an example to be followed in good manners and in the way of guidance, which guides by what is better, avoiding harshness and severity in speech and the ill-treatment of denouncing what the sinner does.
3- Disputation is blameworthy except in the cause of truth:
In His saying «ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا» is an allusion to what is contained in blameworthy disputation, aimed at refuting the truth and extinguishing the light of Allah. As for disputation about the verses to remove their difficulty, resolve what is obscure in them, and contend with scholars in deriving their meanings, the ways of parsing them and the excellence of their exposition, that is commendable, indeed required and obligatory. On this basis comes the saying of the Prophet ﷺ:
«Disputation in the Qur'an is disbelief.» He cited it in the indefinite, in order to distinguish between one disputation and another.
4- The badal in His saying «إنهم من أصحاب النار»:
We parsed «انهم من أصحاب النار» as a badal of كلمة ربك without clarifying the type of badal. It appears that it can be a badal muṭābiq (congruent) or a badal ishtimāl (inclusion). If we look at the wording, it is congruent, because its referent is identical with the referent of the badal; if we consider the meaning, it is a badal of inclusion, because its meaning is His threat to them and His eternal decree of their wretchedness.

dervis-irab:36-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَرْحاً): The ṣarḥ, as in al-Miṣbāḥ, is a single house built on its own, tall and massive. In al-Kashshāf he said: "The ṣarḥ is the conspicuous building that is not hidden from the onlooker even from afar; they derived it from ṣaraḥa al-shayʾ when it appeared. This root is remarkable in its signification, in that in all its derivatives it indicates appearance and clarity. They said: laban ṣarīḥ: milk whose froth has gone and which has become pure; ʿarabī ṣarīḥ, from ʿarab ṣurahāʾ: not of mixed stock; nasab ṣarīḥ (pure lineage); kaʾs ṣirāḥ: a cup not mixed; ṣarraḥat al-khamra: the froth went from the wine; laqītuhu muṣāraḥatan: openly; ṣarraḥa al-nahār: its clouds went and its sun shone. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said, describing a wolf:
إذا امتلّ يعدو قلت ظلّ طخاءة ... ذرى الريح في أعقاب يوم مصرح
(When he sped off running, I said: a shadow of cloud, the wind scattered it in the wake of a clear day.)
He said ṣarraḥa bi-mā fī nafsihi (he spoke out openly what was in his soul), he built a ṣarḥ and ṣurūḥ, and he sat in the ṣarḥa of his house, i.e. in its courtyard."
(الْأَسْبابَ): plural of «سبب». The «أسباب السموات» are its ascents, or its regions, or its doors. The sabab is also the rope, and what one uses to reach something else; Zuhayr combined the two in his saying:
ومن هاب أسباب المنايا ينلنه ... وإن يرق أسباب السماء بسلم
(Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he climbs the ways of heaven by a ladder.)
The sabab is also among the segments of poetry: a vowelled letter and a silent letter, or two vowelled letters; the first is called light and the second heavy."
(تَبابٍ): loss and humiliation. In al-Qāmūs: "al-tabb, al-tabab, al-tabāb, al-tabīb and al-tatbīb: diminution and loss; tabban lahu (ruin to him), and tabban tabīban as an emphasis."
(لا جَرَمَ): its discussion has preceded and further detail will come in the section of Benefits.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يا هامانُ ابْنِ لِي صَرْحاً لَعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ الْأَسْبابَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «قال فرعون»: a verb and an agent; «يا» is a vocative particle; «هامان» is a singular vocative, indeclinable on ḍamma; «ابن» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, its agent latent, its implied form being "you", and the clause is the content of Pharaoh's saying; «لي» is attached to an omitted ḥāl, or to «ابن»; «صرحا» is a direct object; «لعل» and its noun, and the clause «أبلغ الأسباب» is the khabar of «لعل». (أَسْبابَ السَّماواتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلى إِلهِ مُوسى وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ كاذِباً) «أسباب السموات» is a badal of «الأسباب», a total substitute (badal kull min kull); the benefit of the badal is that when a thing is first left vague and then made clear, it magnifies its importance, and this is what Pharaoh intended. «فأطلع»: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; «أطلع» is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ of causation, as the answer to the command, which is «ابن», or the answer to the hope, which is «لعلي أبلغ»; it has also been read with raising, the fāʾ being a conjunction, so that it enters the scope of the hope; more discussion will come in the section of Benefits. «إلى إله موسى» is attached to «أطلع». «وإني»: the wāw is a conjunction, then «إن» and its noun and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «أظنه» is an imperfect verb, the hāʾ a first direct object and «كاذبا» a second direct object; the clause is the khabar of «إن».
(وَكَذلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ وَصُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; «زين» is a passive past verb; «لفرعون» is attached to «زين»; «سوء عمله» is the deputy agent; «صد» is conjoined to «زين», a passive past verb, read with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the ṣād, both readings being among the seven; «عن السبيل» is attached to «صد». (وَما كَيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إِلَّا فِي تَبابٍ) The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; «ما» is negative; «كيد فرعون» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «في تباب» is the khabar of «كيد».
(وَقالَ الَّذِي آمَنَ يا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ) Conjoined to what precedes; «قال الذي»: a past verb and an agent, and the clause «آمن» is a ṣila; «يا قوم» is a vocative whose i'rab has preceded; «اتبعون» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person, omitted because it is among the redundant yāʾs (yāʾāt al-zawāʾid), is in the position of accusative as an object; «أهدكم» is an imperfect verb jussive because it is the answer to a request, its jussive marking being the dropping of the weak letter, the agent being latent, its implied form being "I", and the kāf a direct object; «سبيل الرشاد» is a second direct object or accusative by removal of the preposition; «الرشاد» is a noun for the maṣdar of «رشد».
(يا قَوْمِ إِنَّما هذِهِ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا مَتاعٌ وَإِنَّ الْآخِرَةَ هِيَ دارُ الْقَرارِ) The secret of repeating the vocative and of its being joined with the wāw in the third vocative will come in the section of Rhetoric. «إنما»: «إن» with the restrictive «ما» (kāffa and makfūfa); «هذه» is a mubtadaʾ, «الحياة» a badal, «الدنيا» an adjective and «متاع» the khabar. «وإن الآخرة»: «إن» and its noun; «هي» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; «دار القرار» is the khabar of «إن» or the khabar of «هي», and the clause is the khabar of «إن». (مَنْ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةً فَلا يُجْزى إِلَّا مِثْلَها) «من» is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, a mubtadaʾ; «عمل» is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; «سيئة» is a direct object; the fāʾ is a link; «لا» is negative; «يجزى» is a passive imperfect verb whose deputy agent is latent, its implied form being "he"; «إلا» is a particle of restriction and «مثلها» is the second object of «يجزى». (وَمَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «عمل» is a past verb, the protasis; «صالحا» is a direct object or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "righteous deed"; «من ذكر» is a ḥāl; «أو أنثى» is conjoined to «من ذكر»; «وهو مؤمن»: the wāw is circumstantial, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «مؤمن» a khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(فَأُولئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ يُرْزَقُونَ فِيها بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ) The fāʾ is a link; «أولئك» is a demonstrative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «يدخلون الجنة» is its khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the clause «يرزقون» is a ḥāl, with the wāw as deputy agent; «فيها» is a ḥāl; «بغير» is an adjective of the omitted direct object, i.e. "they are provisioned with ample provision, without reckoning and without liability". (وَيا قَوْمِ ما لِي أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى النَّجاةِ وَتَدْعُونَنِي إِلَى النَّارِ) Conjoined to what precedes; «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «لي» is its khabar; the clause «أدعوكم» is circumstantial; «إلى النجاة» is attached to «أدعوكم»; «وتدعونني إلى النار» is conjoined to «أدعوكم إلى النجاة». (تَدْعُونَنِي لِأَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَأُشْرِكَ بِهِ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ) The clause «تدعونني» is a badal, and the clause «وتدعونني» stands as an explanation of reason (taʿlīl); «لأكفر»: the lām is for reason, and «أكفر» is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied «أن» after the lām of reason, the agent being latent, its implied form being "I"; «بالله» is attached to «أكفر»; «وأشرك» is conjoined to «لأكفر»; «ما» is a direct object, and the clause «ليس لي به علم» is a ṣila; «ليس» is a past defective verb, «لي» its fronted khabar, «به» is attached to «علم», and «علم» is the postponed noun of «ليس».
(وَأَنَا أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى الْعَزِيزِ الْغَفَّارِ) The wāw is a conjunction; «أنا» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «أدعوكم» is the khabar; «إلى العزيز الغفار» is attached to «أدعوكم». (لا جَرَمَ أَنَّما تَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَعْوَةٌ فِي الدُّنْيا وَلا فِي الْآخِرَةِ) «لا» is negative and «جرم» is a past verb meaning "it was right and necessary"; «أن» and what is in its scope is the agent of «جرم», i.e. the falsity of his call was right and necessary; «أن» and its noun; by rights it should be written separately, because «ما» is a relative noun meaning "that which", but it was written joined following the Sunna of the muṣḥaf; the clause «تدعونني» is a ṣila and «إليه» is attached to «تدعونني»; the clause «ليس» is the khabar of «أن»; «له» is the fronted khabar of «ليس» and «دعوة» its postponed noun; «في الدنيا» is an adjective, and «ولا في الآخرة» is conjoined to «في الدنيا».
(وَأَنَّ مَرَدَّنا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَأَنَّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ هُمْ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ) Conjoined to what precedes; «أن» and its noun, and «إلى الله» is its khabar; «وأن المسرفين» is also a conjunction; «هم» is a separating pronoun with no position, or a mubtadaʾ; «أصحاب النار» is the khabar of «أن» or the khabar of «هم», and the clause is the khabar of «أن». (فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ ما أَقُولُ لَكُمْ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent (fāʾ faṣīḥa); the sīn is a particle of futurity; «تذكرون» is an imperfect verb with the wāw as agent; «ما» is a direct object, and the clause «أقول» is a ṣila; «لكم» is attached to «أقول»; «وأفوض» is a conjunction; «أمري» is a direct object, and «إلى الله» is attached to «أفوض»; i.e. when the punishment descends upon you.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبادِ) «إن» and its noun; «بصير» is its khabar; «بالعباد» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «بصير». (فَوَقاهُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِ ما مَكَرُوا وَحاقَ بِآلِ فِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ الْعَذابِ) The fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element required by the context, i.e. when they threatened him with killing and in fact intended it, he fled from them and took refuge in caves and mountain passes; they sought him but could not get at him, so Allah protected him. «وقاه الله»: a past verb, a fronted object and a postponed agent; «سيئات» is a second direct object or accusative by removal of the preposition; «ما» is a maṣdar particle or a relative, i.e. the evils of their plotting against him, or the evils of that which they plotted against him; «حاق» is a past verb; «بآل فرعون» is attached to «حاق»; «سوء العذاب» is the agent. (النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا) «النار» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it", meaning the evil of the punishment; it may also be parsed as a badal of «سوء العذاب», and it may be parsed as a mubtadaʾ with the clause «يعرضون» as khabar; on the first two aspects the clause «يعرضون» is parsed as a ḥāl; «النار» has also been read with accusative, by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), by an omitted verb; «عليها» is attached to «يعرضون»; «غدوا وعشيا» are two adverbials, also attached to «يعرضون».
(وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ الْعَذابِ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted saying, i.e. "it is said to them on the day the Hour arises", and the clause «أدخلوا» is the content of the saying; it may also be attached to «أدخلوا», i.e. "enter on the day the Hour arises"; on these two aspects the full stop is at his saying «وعشيا». It may also be conjoined to the two preceding adverbials, in which case it is attached to «يعرضون», and on this aspect the stop is at «الساعة», and «أدخلوا» is the content of an implied saying, i.e. "it is said to them thus and thus"; «أدخلوا» is an imperative from «أدخل»; «آل فرعون» is a first direct object and «أشد العذاب» a second direct object. It has also been read «ادخلوا» with a hamzat al-waṣl, from «دخل يدخل», in which case «آل فرعون» is a vocative with the vocative particle dropped, and «أشد العذاب» is a direct object.

* Rhetoric:
In the repetition of the address to his people there is emphasis in alerting, challenging, rapping the staff, sincerity of counsel, and rousing from the slumber of heedlessness; it is as though it grieved him that they should become targets of the sorrowful end to which they will come, and as though he were wavering in gentleness toward them, for what grieves them grieves him and what harms them harms him, for they are his people in any case, while they have been bewildered in the mazes of heedlessness. This stance has already been explained in the counsel of Abraham to his father, when he repeated his advice to him gently, in his saying:
«يا أبت» repeatedly.
The wāw was brought in the third vocative, in contrast, because the second vocative stands as a clarification and explanation of the first, so it was given its ruling in the wāw's not entering it, whereas the third enters upon speech that is not of that standing.

* Benefits:
1- In the accusative of his saying «فأطلع» there are three aspects:
a- It is the answer to the command, which is his saying «ابن لي», so it is put in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ in its answer; an example in poetry is the saying of Abū al-Najm al-ʿIjlī:
يا ناق سيري عنقا فسيحا ... إلى سليمان فنستريحا
(O she-camel, go at a wide, easy pace to Sulaymān, that we may rest.)
b- It is the answer to the hope; to this al-Zamakhsharī inclined; he said: "«فأطلع» has been read in the accusative, as the answer to the hope, likening hope to wish."
c- It is conjoined on the basis of supposition (tawahhum), because the khabar of «لعل» very often came joined with «أن» in verse and prose; so whoever put it in the accusative supposed that the raised verb falling as khabar is accusative with «أن»; conjunction on supposition is frequent though not analogical.
2- «لا جرم»:
We expanded the discussion in Hūd on «لا جرم» and gave the many aspects concerning it; and we chose in the i'rab what al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and the majority of the Basrans held, so «لا» is a rejection of what his people called him to, and «جرم» means "earned", i.e. their calling him to it earned the falsity of his call, i.e. nothing resulted from that except the appearance of the falsity of his call. It is also possible that «لا جرم» is like «لا بد», from «الجرم», which is cutting: as you say «لا بد لك أن تفعل», where «البد» is from «التبديد», which is dispersal, its meaning being "you have no separation from doing such-and-such", so likewise «لا جرم» means "there is no cutting off of the falsity of the call of the idols; rather it is false forever".

dervis-irab:7-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ): الذين is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يحملون العرش its ṣila; ومن حوله is conjoined to الذين, and حوله is an adverbial attached to an omitted ṣila of الذين; the clause يسبحون بحمد ربهم is the khabar of الذين; and بحمد are two [elements] attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "bound up with praise". ويؤمنون به is conjoined to يسبحون. The inquiry into the meaning of the bearers of the Throne and who they are is to be found in the longer works. (وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وَعِلْماً): ويستغفرون is conjoined to what precedes; للذين are two [elements] attached to يستغفرون; the clause آمنوا is a ṣila; ربنا is a muḍāf vocative with the vocative particle omitted, and it is the content of an omitted saying, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying". وسعت is a verb and agent; كل شيء is a direct object; and رحمة and علما are two tamyīz (specifications). The tamyīz here is transferred from the agent, i.e. "Your mercy encompassed everything and Your knowledge encompassed everything".
(فَاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ): the فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; اغفر is an imperative verb with "you" as agent; للذين are two [elements] attached to اغفر; the clause تابوا is a ṣila. The meaning: "forgive those from whom You know repentance and following of the straight path". واتبعوا سبيلك is conjoined to للذين تابوا. وقهم: ق is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the weak letter; the ه is a first direct object and عذاب الجحيم a second direct object. (رَبَّنا وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدْتَهُمْ وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبائِهِمْ وَأَزْواجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ): ربنا is a muḍāf vocative with the vocative particle omitted; وأدخلهم is conjoined to what precedes; أدخلهم is an imperative verb of supplication, the agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", the ه a first direct object, and جنات عدن a second direct object by extension. التي is an adjective and the clause وعدتهم the ṣila of التي. من is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object of أدخلهم or to the object of وعدتهم. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: «Its accusative [comes] from two places: if you wish, from the pronoun in أدخلهم, and if you wish, from the pronoun in وعدتهم; and the clause صلح is a ṣila.» The first is preferable. And من آبائهم and what is conjoined to it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): inna and its noun; أنت is a mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); العزيز الحكيم are two khabars of أنت and the sentence is the khabar of إنك, or [they are] two khabars of إن, and أنت has no grammatical position, as was said earlier. (وَقِهِمُ السَّيِّئاتِ وَمَنْ تَقِ السَّيِّئاتِ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمْتَهُ): the و is a conjunction; وقهم is an imperative verb, with a latent agent whose implied form is "you", and a direct object; السيئات is a second direct object; the و is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun that jazms, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; تق is the protasis, jussive, its jussive marker being the omission of the weak letter; السيئات is a direct object; يومئذ is an adverbial attached to تق; إذ is annexed to يوم, and the tanwīn is a substitute for an omitted sentence, intended from the preceding speech, i.e. "the day when You admit whom You will to Paradise and whom You will to the Fire". The فاء links the apodosis; قد is a particle of affirmation; رحمته is a verb, agent and object; and the clause has no grammatical position. (وَذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, هو is a second mubtadaʾ, and الفوز العظيم is the khabar. It is also possible to parse هو as a pronoun of separation with no position. The reference is to the mercy mentioned and the protection from evil deeds.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم» there is a curious art among the arts of rhetoric, called «al-isjāl baʿd al-mughālaṭa» (the guarantee after the feint). It is that the speaker aims at a goal from the one he praises, and so he brings words that affirm that the goal has been reached, as a guarantee from him against the one praised. The explanation is that he stipulates a condition whose occurrence entails the occurrence of that goal, then reports its occurrence as a feint, even though it has not yet occurred, so that what is conditional upon it may occur. The isjāl may also occur without a feint, and this is the type that occurs in the Noble Book; its discussion and an example have already been given in Āl ʿImrān. As for the first type, it occurs in poetry, as in the saying of Ibn Nubāta al-Saʿdī:
جاء الشتاء وما عندي له عدد ... إلا ارتعادي وتصفيقي بأسناني
(Winter has come and I have no provision for it, except my shivering and the chattering of my teeth.)
فإن هلكت فمولانا يكفنني ... هبني هلكت فهبني بعض أكفاني
(If I perish, my patron will shroud me — suppose I have perished; then grant me some of my shrouds.)

dervis-irab:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُنادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ مَقْتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): a resumptive discourse, introduced to begin explaining the states of the disbelievers after their entry into the Fire. إن and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين; the clause ينادون is the khabar of إن; ينادون is a passive imperfect verb and the و is the deputy agent. Those who call out are the angels, after the disbelievers have loathed themselves while being scorched by the Fire of Hell. The لام is the lām of inception; مقت الله is a mubtadaʾ, the annexation being that of a maṣdar to its agent, the direct object being omitted, i.e. "you" (إياكم); أكبر is the khabar; من مقتكم are two [elements] attached to أكبر; and أنفسكم is the object of مقتكم. (إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى الْإِيمانِ فَتَكْفُرُونَ): إذ is an adverbial attached to مقت الله, even though the khabar intervenes between them, because latitude is allowed with adverbials that is not allowed with others. Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade this, for the reason given, and made the adverbial attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He loathed you when you were called". The clause تدعون is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; تدعون is a passive imperfect verb and the و is the deputy agent; and إلى الإيمان are two [elements] attached to تدعون. فتكفرون: the فاء is a conjunction, and تكفرون is an imperfect verb nominative by the presence of the nūn. The meaning derived from the verse is that when they are thrust into the depths of the Fire and taste the terror of burning in it, they break out in mutual blame, hurl accusations at one another, and each casts the blame on the other. Then they are called from a far-off place: Allah's loathing of you, or of your own souls that incite to evil, [was greater] when you were called in the world through the prophets and did not lend an ear, and paid no heed to counsel and guidance, heedless in obeying your unruly desires.
(قالُوا رَبَّنا أَمَتَّنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ فَاعْتَرَفْنا بِذُنُوبِنا فَهَلْ إِلى خُرُوجٍ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ): قالوا is a verb and agent; ربنا is a muḍāf vocative with the vocative particle omitted; أمتنا is a past verb, the ت is the agent and نا an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as direct object; اثنتين is a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose number takes the place of the maṣdar, i.e. "two deaths"; and likewise وأحييتنا اثنتين. اعترفنا is a verb and agent, and بذنوبنا are two [elements] attached to اعترفنا. فهل: the فاء is a conjunction, and هل is an interrogative particle; إلى خروج is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition; and سبيل is genitive in form, nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (ذلِكُمْ بِأَنَّهُ إِذا دُعِيَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ كَفَرْتُمْ): ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the punishment; بأنه is the khabar; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of a condition; the clause دعي is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; الله is the deputy agent; وحده is a ḥāl; the clause كفرتم has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of إذا; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of أنه. What is meant is "you disbelieved in tawḥīd (the Oneness)". (وَإِنْ يُشْرَكْ بِهِ تُؤْمِنُوا فَالْحُكْمُ لِلَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْكَبِيرِ): the و is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يشرك is the protasis, jussive, an imperfect passive verb; به takes the place of the deputy agent; تؤمنوا is the apodosis; and the فاء is a conjunction, because this speech is part of what is said to them in the Hereafter. الحكم is a mubtadaʾ, لله its khabar, and العلي الكبير are two adjectives.

* Rhetoric:
1- Mursal metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal):
In His saying «ربنا أمتنا اثنتين» is a majāz mursal, because what is meant by the two deaths is, first, their being created dead, and second, their being made to die when their appointed terms end; and what is meant by the two lives is the first life and the life of the Resurrection. He, Glorified, made this clear in His saying: «وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم». So in calling their creation as dead a "causing to die" there is majāz, because it is in consideration of what they had been. Al-Zamakhsharī explained this with the fullest clarity in his enjoyable passage on this point, which we quote verbatim for its worth. He said: «If you ask: how is it right to call their creation as dead "causing to die"? I say: just as it is right for you to say, "Glory to Him who made the body of the gnat small and the body of the elephant large", and your saying to the well-digger, "narrow the mouth of the well and widen its bottom", when there is no transfer from smallness to largeness, or the reverse, or from narrowness to width, or the reverse; rather what is meant is the bringing into being upon those attributes. The reason for its soundness is that largeness and smallness are both possible for one and the same made thing, with no preponderance for either, and likewise narrowness and width. So when the maker chooses one of the two possibilities, being equally able to do either, he has turned the made thing away from the other possibility, and makes his turning it away from it like transferring it from it.»
2- Interrogation in the sense of despair:
In His saying «فهل إلى خروج من سبيل» there is in this interrogation a despairing hopelessness and extreme impossibility, as though, from the excess of what they endure, they wish to get out of this enveloping grief and entrenched terror — but what a wish! It is the wish of one overcome by despair and hopelessness. The indefiniteness of خروج indicates any exit whatever, whether swift or slow. They say that only as an excuse and out of bewilderment, and so the answer came accordingly, namely His saying «ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم», meaning that the cause goes back to your disbelief, so do not hope for the removal of what you are in, for it is your own crime and the blame falls on yourselves. Poets have clung to the hems of this wonderful expression; one of them said:
هل إلى نجد وصول ... وعلى الخيف نزول
(Is there a way of reaching Najd, and a halting at al-Khayf?)
Their intent is that this is a matter in which despair has overcome desire, and the one who wishes has been kept from what he wishes.

dervis-irab:13-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْآزِفَةِ): the Resurrection; it is so called because of its اُزوف, i.e. its nearness, from أزف الرحيل, meaning "the departure drew near". In al-Miṣbāḥ: «أزف الرحيل أزفا (pattern "taʿiba") and أزوفا: it drew close and near; and أزفت الآزفة: the Resurrection.» In al-Asās: أزف الرحيل:
it drew near and hastened; from it, "he came walking the azfā", on the pattern of al-jamzā, as if it were from al-wazīf, the hamza replacing a wāw; and "the nearness of their departure distressed me", and "their departure drew near"....
and الآزفة is the Resurrection because of its nearness. Hudba said:
وبادرها مصر العشيّة قرمها ... ذر البيت يغشاه من القرّ آزف
[Translator's note: the verse is given here in the source's wording, whose text is evidently corrupt in places; it is quoted as an instance of the use of آزف, "near, pressing", and no continuous English rendering is attempted.]
(الْحَناجِرِ): in al-Mukhtār: «الحنجرة with fatḥa, and الحنجور with ḍamma: the gullet (al-ḥulqūm).» In al-Qāmūs: «الحنجور is the small chest (safat), a bottle for powder (dharīra), and the gullet, like الحنجرة; and الحناجر is its plural.»

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمْ آياتِهِ وَيُنَزِّلُ لَكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ رِزْقاً): a resumptive discourse, introduced to demonstrate that judgment belongs to Him, Glorified. هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي the khabar; the clause يريكم is a ṣila; آياته is a direct object; وينزل لكم is conjoined to يريكم; and من السماء are two [elements] attached to ينزل, to indicate the renewal of the showing and sending down, and their continuity and persistence. (وَما يَتَذَكَّرُ إِلَّا مَنْ يُنِيبُ): the و is a conjunction; ما is negative; يتذكر is an imperfect nominative verb; إلا is a particle of restriction; من is the agent; and the clause ينيب is a ṣila. (فَادْعُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ): the فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if the matter is as mentioned, then call upon". The Majestic Name is a direct object; مخلصين is a ḥāl; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مخلصين; الدين is a direct object; the و is circumstantial; لو is conditional; and كره الكافرون is a verb and agent, the direct object omitted, i.e. "your sincerity" or "your calling". (رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجاتِ ذُو الْعَرْشِ يُلْقِي الرُّوحَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ لِيُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ): رفيع الدرجات is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and ذو العرش a second khabar, and the clause يلقي الروح a third khabar, i.e. [the mubtadaʾ is] Allah. ومن أمره are two [elements] attached to يلقي, or to an omitted ḥāl from الروح, i.e. revelation — that is, while it arises from His command. By الروح is meant revelation; the reason for naming it so will come in the section on rhetoric. وعلى من are two [elements] attached to يلقي; the clause يشاء is a ṣila; and من عباده is a ḥāl. ولينذر: the lām is causal; ينذر is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يلقي; and the agent of ينذر may be Allah, or the Spirit, or "whom He wills"; يوم is a direct object of لينذر and التلاق is its muḍāf ilayhi; the yāʾ is omitted following the orthography of the muṣḥaf, and it is also read with the yāʾ retained. The Day of Resurrection is called the Day of Meeting (yawm al-talāqī) because creatures meet one another on it.
(يَوْمَ هُمْ بارِزُونَ لا يَخْفى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ): يوم is a badal of يوم التلاق (a total substitute for the whole); هم is a mubtadaʾ and بارزون its khabar; the nominal sentence is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; so the vowel of يوم is a vowel of declension, according to the well-known view; this will be set out in the section on benefits. The clause لا يخفى is a ḥāl from the pronoun of بارزون, or a second khabar; it is also said that it is resumptive. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred the ḥāl reading, and perhaps he is right. على الله are two [elements] attached to يخفى; منهم is a ḥāl, because in origin it was an adjective of شيء; and شيء is the agent of يخفى. (لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ): a narration of what will be asked on that day and how it will be answered; the sentence is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. He, the Exalted, says it and answers Himself. The saying is conjoined to what precedes, or is resumptive in answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "What will happen then?" and it was said: "It will be said: To whom belongs the dominion?" لمن is a fronted khabar and الملك a postponed mubtadaʾ; اليوم is an adverbial attached to الملك; لله is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the dominion belongs to Allah"; and الواحد القهار are two adjectives of لله. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «A caller will call out and say: "To whom belongs the dominion this day?" and the people of the gathering-place will answer him: "To Allah, the One, the Irresistible."»
(الْيَوْمَ تُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ): the adverbial is attached to تجزى, and the speech is a completion of what is said; تجزى is a passive imperfect verb and كل نفس the deputy agent; بما are two [elements] attached to تجزى; and ما is a relative or a temporal (ẓarfiyya). (لا ظُلْمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ): لا is the lā of generic negation, and ظلم is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa; اليوم is an adverbial attached to an omitted khabar; إن with its noun and khabar; and the sentence gives the reason for the absence of injustice, i.e. no reckoning occupies Him from another reckoning, so He is swift in His reckoning, just in His judgment. (وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْآزِفَةِ إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَناجِرِ كاظِمِينَ): the و is a conjunction linking to what precedes; وأنذرهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; يوم الآزفة is a second direct object; إذ is a badal of يوم الآزفة; القلوب is a mubtadaʾ; لدى الحناجر is an adverbial attached to an omitted khabar; the sentence is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; and كاظمين is a ḥāl of القلوب. The hearts, in being plural-ed with yāʾ and nūn (the sound masculine plural), have been treated as their owners. Al-Zamakhsharī's account will come in the section on rhetoric. (ما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَلا شَفِيعٍ يُطاعُ)
The sentence is a ḥāl from the owners of the hearts; ما is a Hijazi negative, or inoperative; للظالمين is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition; حميم is the postponed noun of ما, or a mubtadaʾ; ولا شفيع is conjoined to حميم; and the clause يطاع is an adjective of شفيع. In the speech there is a majāz whose detail will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «يلقي الروح من أمره» there is a majāz mursal, because what is meant by الروح is revelation. Revelation is called a spirit because it flows into hearts as spirits flow into bodies. So it is a majāz mursal whose relation is causality. Al-Zamakhsharī made it an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), and that is not far-fetched.
2- Representation (al-tamthīl):
In His saying «إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين» is a representative metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), to embody the terror of that day on which they will be nearing the Fire. Then their hearts rise from their places and stick in their throats; they neither come out, so that they die and are at rest, nor return to their places, so that they could breathe deeply and find relief; rather they lodge across like a bone in the throat.
3- Reversal of the apparent (ʿaks al-ẓāhir):
In His saying «ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع» is a reversal of the apparent; this art has been mentioned more than once, since they have no intercessor at all, let alone an obeyed one.
4- Al-Zamakhsharī's statement on كاظمين:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: by what is كاظمين made accusative? I say: it is a ḥāl from the owners of the hearts in meaning, because the meaning is "when their hearts are at their throats, they suppressing [their anguish] over them". It may also be a ḥāl from the hearts, with the hearts suppressing grief and distress within them while reaching the throats. The كاظم was given the sound plural only because He described them with suppression (kaẓm), which is among the acts of rational beings, as the Exalted said:
"I saw them prostrating to me" and said: "so their necks remained humbled to it".»

* Benefits:
Annexation of time words to sentences:
It is permissible, for a time word annexed to a sentence, to be declined according to the origin or to be indeclinable. If what follows it is an indeclinable verb, indeclinability is preferable, for the sake of harmony, or because the adverbial then resembles the conditional particle in making the sentence following it dependent on it and on something else, as in the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا ... وقلت: ألما أصح والشيب وازع
(At the time when I rebuked grey hair on account of youth and said: "Have I not become sober, with grey hair a restraint?")
It is reported "ʿalā ḥīni" with the genitive, as declined, and "ʿalā ḥīna" with fatḥa, as indeclinable, and the latter is preferable because it is annexed to what is indeclinable by origin, namely عاتبت. Indeclinability may also be an incidental state, and the same applies, as in the saying:
لأجتذبن منهن قلبي تحلما ... على حين يستصبين كل حليم
(I will wrest my heart from them in forbearance, at a time when they allure every forbearing man.)
It is reported with the genitive of حين as declined, and with its fatḥa as indeclinable, because it is annexed to what is indeclinable, namely يستصبين, for it is an imperfect verb indeclinable on sukūn through its connection with the feminine nūn; its past is استصبيت فلانا when you put him among the boys. If what follows it is a declinable imperfect verb or a nominal sentence, declension is preferable to indeclinability, and it is obligatory for the Basrans because of the lack of harmony. We said "preferable" because Nāfiʿ, one of the great readers, read «هذا يوم ينفع» with fatḥa as indeclinable, not as declined. The majority of the Basrans answered that the fatḥa in it is not a fatḥa of indeclinability but a fatḥa of declension, like that in "I kept silent on Thursday", and for that reason they held that the demonstrative must not refer to the day, otherwise a thing would be an adverbial of itself. Hence al-Fārisī and Ibn Mālik held declension to be preferable. He said in al-Khulāṣa:
وقبل فعل معرب أو مبتدأ ... أعرب ومن بنى فلن يفندا
(Before a declinable verb or a mubtadaʾ, decline it; and whoever makes it indeclinable will not be faulted.)

dervis-irab:19-22.t:
* I'rab:
(يَعْلَمُ خائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ وَما تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ): the sentence is a fourth khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ that was predicated with رفيع الدرجات and what follows; or it is one of the khabars of "هو الذي يريكم"; or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; or it is causal with no grammatical position. يعلم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent whose implied form is "he", i.e. Allah the Exalted; خائنة الأعين is a direct object, the annexation having the sense of "from" (min), i.e. the treacherous one among the eyes. On this view خائنة is an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "the treacherous eye"; it is also possible that الخائنة is a maṣdar like العاقبة and الكاذبة, i.e. "He knows the treachery of the eyes". More discussion of this expression will come in the section on rhetoric. The و is a conjunction; ما is conjoined to خائنة الأعين; and the clause تخفي الصدور is the ṣila of ما.
(وَاللَّهُ يَقْضِي بِالْحَقِّ): the و is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يقضي بالحق its khabar; and بالحق are two [elements] attached to يقضي, or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "bound up with it".
(وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لا يَقْضُونَ بِشَيْءٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ): the و is a conjunction; الذين is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يدعون a ṣila; من دونه are two [elements] attached to يدعون; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "they call upon them besides Him", in the sense of "they worship them"; the clause لا يقضون بشيء is the khabar of الذين. إن and its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation; and السميع البصير is the khabar of إن, or of "هو" and of إن.
(أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the hamza is for rebuking interrogation; He rebukes them for not taking lessons from the states of others. The و is a conjunction linking to an implied clause that the context requires, i.e. "Were they heedless, and did they not travel?" لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; يسيروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; and في الأرض are two [elements] attached to يسيروا. فينظروا: the فاء is causal or a conjunction, and ينظروا is accusative by an implied أن after the causal فاء, or jussive, conjoined to يسيروا. كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a fronted khabar of كان; عاقبة is its noun; the sentence is in the position of accusative as the object of لينظروا; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of الذين; and من قبلهم is the khabar of كانوا. (كانُوا هُمْ أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَآثاراً فِي الْأَرْضِ): كان and its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation with no position; and أشد is its khabar. The pronoun of separation may enter between a definite and an indefinite, though it occurs only between two definites, because the indefinite here — أشد — is equivalent to a definite in that ال cannot enter it, since a comparative accompanied by من does not take ال. منهم are two [elements] attached to أشد; قوة is a tamyīz; آثارا is conjoined to قوة; and في الأرض is an adjective of آثارا. Al-Zamakhsharī made it accusative by an implied [verb or word], i.e. "more in traces", as in the saying «متقلدا سيفا ورمحا» (girded with a sword and a spear). (فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَما كانَ لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ واقٍ): the فاء is a conjunction; أخذهم الله is a verb, direct object and agent; بذنوبهم are two [elements] attached to أخذهم, and the باء is causal, i.e. "because of their sins". The و is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; لهم is its fronted khabar; من الله are two [elements] attached to واق; من is a redundant preposition; and واق is genitive in form, nominative in position as the postponed noun of كان.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَكَفَرُوا فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the seizing; the باء is a causal preposition; أن and what it governs is in the position of genitive by the باء; and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of ذلك. أن and its noun; the clause تأتيهم is the khabar of كانت, whose noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she"; رسلهم is the agent of تأتيهم; بالبينات are two [elements] attached to تأتيهم; فكفروا is conjoined to تأتيهم; and فأخذهم الله is conjoined to His saying فكفروا.
(إِنَّهُ قَوِيٌّ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): a reason for the seizing; إن and its noun; قوي is a first khabar and شديد العقاب a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The art of al-farāʾid (the unique gems):
In His saying «يعلم خائنة الأعين» is the art of al-farāʾid, which is among the arts of badīʿ and pertains to eloquence (faṣāḥa) rather than to rhetoric (balāgha). It is that the speaker brings into his speech a word that takes the place of the unique bead (farīda) among the beads of a necklace, the jewel that has no like, which indicates the soundness of his speech, the greatness of his eloquence, the strength of his expression and the authenticity of his Arabic, such that if this word were dropped from the speech, its rarity would be precious to the eloquent. Examples are many in the Qur'an, and many have passed. Here it is in the word «خائنة»: on its own it is easy, acceptable and common on the tongues; but when it was annexed to الأعين, it acquired from the strangeness of the construction an impact on the souls such that nothing like it can be produced, and no one of sound thought and upright mind can hit on anything similar. This word has occupied the great scholars and masters of eloquence, and we shall give some of their statements. Ibn ʿAbbās said: «It is the man who is sitting with the people when a woman passes, and he steals a glance at her.» Mujāhid said: «It is the stealing of the eyes' glance toward what Allah has forbidden.» Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «It is a person's saying "I did not see" when he has seen.» Al-Suddī said: «It is the signalling with the eye.» Sufyān said: «It is the glance after the glance.» Al-Farrāʾ said: «خائنة الأعين is the second glance, and وما تخفي الصدور the first glance.» Ibn ʿAbbās said: «وما تخفي الصدور means: would he commit adultery with her if he were alone with her, or not?» And it is said: «وما تخفي الصدور means what they conceal and keep inwardly.»

dervis-irab:23-27.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): the و is resumptive and the sentence is resumptive, introduced to begin the story of Moses with Pharaoh. The لام is the apodosis of an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; موسى is a direct object; بآياتنا are two [elements] attached to أرسلنا; سلطان is conjoined to بآياتنا; and مبين is an adjective. You may also attach بآياتنا to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "bound up with Our signs", and perhaps that is better. (إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ وَقارُونَ فَقالُوا: ساحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ): إلى فرعون are two [elements] attached to أرسلنا; هامان and قارون are conjoined to فرعون; فقالوا is conjoined to أرسلنا; and ساحر كذاب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is a lying sorcerer". (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ مِنْ عِنْدِنا قالُوا اقْتُلُوا أَبْناءَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ وَاسْتَحْيُوا نِساءَهُمْ): the فاء is resumptive; لما is a temporal adverbial or a conjunctive particle; جاءهم is a verb, direct object and latent agent; بالحق are two [elements] attached to جاءهم; من عندنا are two [elements] attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, namely لما. اقتلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn; the و is the agent; the sentence is the content of what was said; أبناء الذين is a direct object; the clause آمنوا is a ṣila; معه is an adverbial of place attached to آمنوا; واستحيوا is conjoined to اقتلوا, i.e. "spare"; and نساءهم is a direct object.
(وَما كَيْدُ الْكافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ): the و is circumstantial; ما is negative; كيد الكافرين is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; and في ضلال is the khabar of كيد. (وَقالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ذَرُونِي أَقْتُلْ مُوسى وَلْيَدْعُ رَبَّهُ): the و is a conjunction; قال فرعون is a past verb and agent; ذروني is an imperative verb, agent and direct object, and the sentence is the content of what was said; أقتل is an imperfect verb jussive because it is the apodosis of a request, with a latent agent whose implied form is "I", referring to the speaker, Pharaoh, because his people kept dissuading him from killing him, making light of his matter and belittling his standing. وليدع: the و is a conjunction; the لام is the lām of command; يدع is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; the intent of the command here is, by his claim, to challenge him as incapable; and ربه is a direct object. (إِنِّي أَخافُ أَنْ يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُمْ أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ فِي الْأَرْضِ الْفَسادَ): the sentence is a reason for his demand to kill Moses; إن and its noun; أن and what is within its scope is the object of أخاف; أن is a maṣdar and accusative particle; يبدل is an imperfect verb accusative by أن; دينكم is a direct object; أو is a conjunction; أن يظهر is conjoined to أن يبدل; في الأرض are two [elements] attached to يظهر; and الفساد is the object of يظهر. (وَقالَ مُوسى إِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِيَوْمِ الْحِسابِ): the و is a conjunction; قال موسى is a verb and agent; إن and its noun; the clause عذت is its khabar, and the sentence is the content of what was said; من كل متكبر are two [elements] attached to عذت; the clause لا يؤمن is an adjective of متكبر; and بيوم الحساب are two [elements] attached to يؤمن.
